title: Trapezius Muscle Work
summary: Gentle palm-and-finger work over the upper shoulder girdle without pressing on the neck or bony structures.
goal: Reduce the subjective feeling of tension in the upper shoulder girdle and encourage relaxation.
imageAlt: Educational diagram of trapezius muscle work without text labels.
startingPosition: The person lies face down or sits comfortably. Keep the shoulders relaxed and the neck neutral.
instructions: Place the palm on the soft part of the upper shoulder.
Use a few gentle strokes from the base of the neck toward the shoulder.
Add small circular movements over the muscle.
If comfortable, gently compress the muscle between the fingers and heel of the hand.
Reduce pressure near the neck and bony landmarks.
direction: From the base of the neck toward the shoulder; local circles stay on soft tissue.
tips: Ask the person to relax the shoulders.
Use less pressure near the base of the neck.
mistakes: Pressure on the side or front of the neck.
warning: Do not perform this technique over acute pain, recent injury, significant inflammation, damaged skin, or when touch increases symptoms. Seek qualified professional advice when uncertain.
